subject: SLO exception request: multi-region failover impact on checkout
messages:

Cc: Maya Rao <contracts@acme-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 16:12:00 +00:00
Subject: Checkout 503 spike and fallback to US — request for SLO exception and logs

Sergio / Monica,

We observed a significant spike in 503s on our EU checkout between 02:04–02:40 UTC this morning. Our telemetry shows a 5.2% error rate on submit calls during that window which triggered our client-side fallback to the US region and added ~300–600ms additional median latency for ~18% of checkout traffic. A few orders were affected and the payments team is seeing chargeback risk on a handful of transactions.

We need Redwood to confirm the exact service availability window (start/end times) per your SLO definitions, provide the evidence bundle (request logs, traces, routing decisions), and confirm whether this incident will be eligible for an SLO exception / credit per our contract. We will share our internal traces; attaching a small sample of request IDs and spans for your reference.

Requested next steps:
- Confirmation of official downtime window and SLO eligibility criteria you will use
- Raw logs + trace bundle (or link to shared drive)
- ETA for a postmortem and preliminary credit estimate

Kevin
Ops Lead, Acme Payments

Subject: Re: Fwd: Checkout 503 spike — please validate routing window

Sergio / Monica — I pulled the traces and infra events. Summary of findings so far:

- Timeline (UTC): 02:03:48 — 02:39:55 
  - At ~02:03:48 we saw a spike of internal routing rejections from the eu-west-1 edge cluster due to an overloaded routing table update process after an autoscaler churn. That caused a gradual increase in 5xx responses from the EU frontdoors and a failover policy kicked in routing traffic to the nearest available region (us-west-2) for some tenants, including Acme.
  - Elevated 503s reached a sustained 5+ minute window starting ~02:06 and persisted intermittently until ~02:38; the worst contiguous interval is ~20 minutes (02:06–02:26) with >4.5% error rate for the checkout route.

- Preliminary SLO eligibility: per our contract SLO definition (sustained 5xx > 1% over a 5-minute window), the incident qualifies for an availability SLO exception for part of the window. Based on initial calculations, ~12 minutes of the interval would be eligible for credit calculation pending exact cross-tenant dedup and whether client-side fallback makes portions not eligible under terms.

- Attachments: I’ve prepared a redwood_prelim_tracebundle_20280402.tar.gz with request-level traces, edge metrics, and routing decision logs. This bundle redacts PII but includes request ids requested by Acme.

- Next steps: 1) Give me permission to publish the sanitized bundle to the secure drive linked to the HubSpot ticket; 2) I’ll hand this to SRE for a full RCA and provide the exact SLO window and credit calc within 48 hours.

Karthik
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
